images.caption: East Tarbet. This is the 'neck' of the Mull of Galloway. A tarbet is a place where a boat could be dragged from one side of a headland or island to the other [which is probably not done much these days]. This side is on Luce Bay, the point on the other side of the headland is on the Irish Sea and is called, somewhat predictably, West Tarbet.

images.filename: Coastal heath in the RSPB reserve - geograph.org.uk - 1725870.jpg
images.caption:
Coastal heath in the RSPB reserve Coastal heathland is a semi-natural habitat that today occurs only in small pockets around Dumfries and Galloway. In the reserve it supports breeding birds such as twite, stonechat, linnet and wheatear.
The sands of Maryport Bay can be seen in the distance on the right.
